Utilities & C Compatibility

On this page

Standard Library Overview ​

The SafeC standard library (std/) covers core utilities, collections, allocators, networking, filesystems, DSP, debugging, and security. Each module is a .h header, plus a .sc implementation for the non-generic parts; generic containers are header-only. #include only ever names .h files — the .sc files are compiled once into libsafec_std.a and linked. Include prelude.h to pull in most modules at once; GUI, encoding, HTTP/RPC/wasm, the real-time scheduler, ML and SIMD are included by their own headers.

c
#include <std/prelude.h>

int main() {
    println("Hello from SafeC stdlib!");
    return 0;
}

Generic Pattern ​

Containers and other value-holding APIs are generic structs and functions, monomorphized per element type. They hand out ?&T references (narrow them with match, .default(x), or std::expect_ref), return ?T when there may be no value, and take typed fn callbacks — the standard library has no void* element or callback parameters. T is written once, on the variable, and the constructor infers it from that target type:

c
#include <std/collections/vec.h>

int main() {
    struct Vec<int> v = std::Vec::new();
    v.push(42);
    v.push(100);
    match (v.get(0UL)) {
        case some(x): *x = *x + 1;      // 43, written in place
        case null:    { }
    }
    int last = v.pop().default(-1);     // 100
    v.free();
    return last == 100 ? 0 : 1;
}

Where a container must hold callbacks with different context types at once (a timer wheel, a widget tree, a VFS mounting several drivers), the slot stores the pair type-erased, but the only way to fill it is a generic method that takes a matching fn(?&T) and ?&T — TimerWheel::add, Widget::on_click, Vfs::mount, TaskScheduler::spawn — so every call is still checked at compile time. The remaining void* declarations in std/ are C ABI boundaries: libc/OS externs, mem.h's raw byte allocator, MMIO base addresses, and GPU/WASM foreign interfaces.

Including the Standard Library ​

Individual modules:

c
#include <std/mem.h>
#include <std/io.h>
#include <std/collections/vec.h>

Most modules at once:

c
#include <std/prelude.h>

When building with the safeguard package manager, the std modules the program includes (and the ones its code calls without an include: new, channels) are compiled into build/deps/libsafec_std.a and linked, with the system libraries they need — or, in a release install, taken from its prebuilt std archive (see Standard Library Modules).

When building manually, put the SafeC checkout on the include path (headers are named <std/...>) and link an archive of all of std — safeguard build of a project with [build] std = "all" makes one (or build it from every std/**/*.sc) — with the system libraries of the modules you use (safeguard std-modules std/x.h lists them):

bash
safec myfile.sc -I /path/to/SafeC -o myfile.ll
clang myfile.ll /path/to/libsafec_std.a -lm -lpthread -o myfile
